question: Which of the following is the olfactory indicator to check the acidic or basic nature of the substance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vanilla essence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vanilla essence:**

 
 
• Vanilla essence is an olfactory indicator, meaning it uses changes in odor to detect acidic or basic substances.
 
• In acidic solutions, vanilla essence retains its characteristic sweet smell.
 
• In basic solutions, the smell of vanilla essence diminishes or disappears.
 
• Olfactory indicators are particularly useful for visually impaired individuals.
 
• The change in odor is due to the reaction of the basic substance with the compounds responsible for the vanilla scent.
 
• This is a qualitative test, and not a quantitative test.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phenolphthalein:**

 
 
• Phenolphthalein is a chemical indicator that changes color depending on the pH of a solution.
 
• It is colorless in acidic solutions and pink in basic solutions.
 
• Phenolphthalein is commonly used in titrations to determine the endpoint of acid-base reactions.
 
• It is a visual indicator, not an olfactory indicator.
 
• The color change happens due to the change in the phenolphthalein molecule structure, due to changes in the pH.
 
 
 
• **Red litmus:**
 
 
• Red litmus paper is a pH indicator that changes color in the presence of basic solutions.
 
• It remains red in acidic solutions and turns blue in basic solutions.
 
• Litmus paper is used to determine whether a solution is acidic or basic.
 
• It is a visual indicator, not an olfactory indicator.
 
• Litmus paper is a natural dye derived from lichens.
 
 
 
• **Methyl orange:**
 
 
• Methyl orange is a pH indicator that changes color depending on the acidity of a solution.
 
• It is red in strongly acidic solutions, orange in moderately acidic solutions, and yellow in neutral or basic solutions.
 
• Methyl orange is commonly used in titrations.
 
• It is a visual indicator, not an olfactory indicator.
 
• The color change happens due to the change in the methyl orange molecule structure, due to changes in the pH.
